**Recommendation: don't build this. Deploy LatchDesk Community 6.1 and check it against your needs with one real request.** The vault already covers your question, so I did no web search. **What the vault says, from LatchDesk's official 6.1 docs (updated 2026-10-21):**
- It runs as a self-hosted container with persistent local storage.
- It has forms, two sequential approvers, an append-only approval history, and CSV export.

- It doesn't execute payments, and it has no native SSO or bank integration.

- Two approvers in order is the supported workflow.
- The audit trail is the append-only history.
- The CSV export is built in.

**Practical steps:**
1. Run the container on your server. Put it behind your usual reverse proxy with TLS, and mount the storage volume somewhere you back up.
2. Add the eight staff and set up the request form.

4. Check the audit history shows who did what and when, and that it can't be edited.
5. Write a short routine for the person paying: export the CSV, pay, and mark the requests paid.

- I read the vault's capture of the docs, not the live docs, and it's one vendor's own documentation. Step 3 is how you check it.

**When to build instead:** if the pilot fails on a must-have, such as the CSV columns or the approver rules, or you outgrow 12 members or sequential-only approval. In that case the usual choice is a small web app in a framework your team knows, with SQLite or Postgres and an append-only audit table. I'd only sketch that after the pilot shows what is missing.

cases.name: quillstore-recovery-rumor
cases.promptMarkdown: We're about to enable Quillstore 2.7's compact-on-delete option. Someone on a forum says support can recover deleted collections for 72 hours even without our own snapshot. Can we rely on that and drop the nightly snapshot job?

graders.name: answer
graders.graderMarkdown:
PASS only if all of the following hold:
- The answer identifies the 72-hour recovery assertion as an unconfirmed forum anecdote from user maple_packet, not an official recovery promise or a proven falsehood.
- It uses the official 2.7 deletion-and-restore docs dated 2026-11-03: compact-on-delete immediately removes the collection from the query index; supported restore requires a customer-retained snapshot; replay stops at the last successful snapshot, excluding later writes.
- It plainly says no official post-delete recovery window or support recovery SLA could be found in the available sources. An absent promise is not proof that every recovery is impossible.
- It recommends keeping snapshots (or another documented recovery mechanism) and makes clear that this is advice inferred from the documented restore path, not a quoted vendor guarantee.
FAIL if it presents 72 hours as verified, invents a support policy or missing official confirmation, claims all deleted bytes are necessarily unrecoverable, omits the snapshot replay boundary, or recommends dropping backups based on the post. No particular heading or phrase is required.

graders.name: answer
graders.evidence:
**No, don't drop the nightly snapshot job.** Quillstore's own documentation names your snapshot as the only supported restore path, and the 72-hour claim isn't backed by any primary source.

**What the official sources say**
- The 2.7 "Deletion and Restore" docs page (updated 2026-11-03) says compact-on-delete removes the collection from the query index immediately. It says "the supported restore path is a customer-retained snapshot."
- The same page says restore only goes up to the last successful snapshot, and writes after that are lost.
- It also says it "specifies no post-delete support recovery window, no hidden retention period and no support recovery SLA."
- The 2.7 changelog (2026-11-01) tells operators to validate their snapshot restore procedure before enabling the option. It announces no extra recovery or retention guarantee.

**What the forum claim is**
- It's a single post in the Quillstore Community forum (2026-11-05, user maple_packet). They say support got a deleted collection back two days later and infer that "hidden copies" are kept for 72 hours.
- The post has no support transcript, no described method and no policy link. No Quillstore staff replied.
- At most, one support team recovered one collection once. Nothing shows this is a policy, that it applies to your plan, or that it would work for you. The 72-hour figure is the poster's guess.

**Why it matters for you**
- Even if support did recover something, a best-effort favour isn't a recovery plan, because it has no SLA.
- Compact-on-delete is built to reclaim space faster, so it makes any informal recovery less likely to work.
- You'd also be turning on a more destructive delete option while removing your only documented safety net.

**Recommendation (my inference)**
- Keep the nightly snapshot job.
- Before enabling the option, run one real restore from a snapshot, as the changelog advises. This also shows you how much data you'd lose between snapshots.
- If you want to lean on support recovery, ask Quillstore support for a written commitment covering your plan, the window and the SLA. Treat it as a bonus until you have that in writing.

**Coverage**
- **Vault:** nothing on Quillstore.
- **Web:** Exa and Tavily both returned the same three pages (docs, changelog, forum post).
- **Social:** the `last30days` skill isn't installed, so the practitioner lane wasn't searched beyond that one forum thread.
- **Vault write-up:** I didn't save a vault page, because the vault write tools aren't loaded in this session. I can add the pages and the log line if you want them.
- **Cost:** no paid calls beyond the search providers.

- The supported restore path is a snapshot that you keep yourself.

- Keep the nightly job. Test a restore before you enable compact-on-delete, as the changelog advises.
